chunks: And the Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

"There is no righteous servant nor prophet who has not prayed in the Mosque of Kufa, to the extent that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey, Gabriel (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know where you are at this moment, O Messenger of Allah? You are opposite the Mosque of Kufa.' He said: 'I said, 'Ask permission for me from my Lord so that I may go to it and pray two rak'ahs in it.' So Allah, Exalted and Glorious, granted him permission. And indeed, its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its rear is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And the obligatory prayer performed in it equals a thousand prayers, and the voluntary prayer equals five hundred prayers. And sitting in it without recitation or remembrance is an act of worship. And if people knew what is in it, they would come to it, even if crawling.'

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ بِهِ: The Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj) of the Prophet
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ كُوفَانَ: The Mosque of Kufa, a prominent in Shia tradition for its virtues

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual virtues and rewards of praying in the Mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the cosmological significance of the Mosque of Kufa by noting that every righteous servant and prophet has prayed there, a status confirmed during the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra) when Gabriel identified its location opposite the Prophet. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, emphasizes the mosque's unique spiritual hierarchy, where its right and rear sides are gardens of Paradise, and even sitting in contemplation is considered an act of worship, underscoring its centrality in Shia devotional geography.
